title: Cleaning and personal care - 123 school
heading: Cleaning and personal care
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.
You learn these terms and calculations by practising. Only use BINAS when the question names a BINAS table.

questions.q: What is natural soap made from?
questions.a: From vegetable and animal oils and fats (synthetic soap: from petroleum products)

questions.q: Which two parts does a soap molecule consist of?
questions.a: A head and a tail

questions.q: Which part of a soap molecule dissolves in water?
questions.a: De kop

questions.q: Which part of a soap molecule dissolves in fat?
questions.a: The tail

questions.q: What type of substance is soap?
questions.a: An emulsifier

questions.q: What does soap do when cleaning?
questions.a: It makes fat and water mix, so that the fat can be rinsed away

questions.q: What is hard water?
questions.a: Water in which a lot of lime is dissolved. Soft water contains little lime.

questions.q: What is soap scum?
questions.a: A white solid that forms when soap reacts with lime

questions.q: Do you need more or less soap with hard water than with soft water?
questions.a: More soap

questions.q: What are cosmetics? Give two examples
questions.a: Products for caring for or beautifying your body. For example shampoo and toothpaste.

questions.q: What is a cream?
questions.a: An emulsion that you rub onto your skin

questions.q: What are the main ingredients of a cream?
questions.a: Water, oil or fat and an emulsifier

questions.q: What are the main ingredients of shampoo?
questions.a: Water, soap and table salt

questions.q: What are the main ingredients of toothpaste?
questions.a: Soap and an abrasive

questions.q: What does the abrasive in toothpaste do?
questions.a: It polishes your teeth clean

questions.q: Which ingredient in toothpaste speeds up the repair of your tooth enamel?
questions.a: Fluoride

questions.q: What is sebum?
questions.a: The thin layer of fat (skin oil) on your skin

questions.q: Why can you not remove sebum with water alone?
questions.a: Sebum is fat and fat does not dissolve in water

questions.q: Why do you need more soap with hard water?
questions.a: Part of the soap reacts with lime to form soap scum. Less active soap is then left.

questions.q: What happens to your skin if you wash away all the sebum?
questions.a: Your skin dries out

questions.q: What does hydrophilic mean?
questions.a: Water-loving: the substance or the part of the molecule dissolves well in water

questions.q: What does hydrophobic mean?
questions.a: Water-fearing: the substance or the part of the molecule does not dissolve in water

questions.q: Which part of a soap molecule is hydrophilic and which part is hydrophobic?
questions.a: The head is hydrophilic, the tail is hydrophobic

questions.q: Why does fat not dissolve in water?
questions.a: Fat is hydrophobic

questions.q: How do soap molecules make it possible for a drop of fat to be rinsed away?
questions.a: The tails are in the fat and the heads stick out into the water

questions.q: What function does water have when washing clothes?
questions.a: Solvent and rinsing agent

questions.q: What pH does an all-purpose cleaner for grease usually have?
questions.a: Higher than 7 (basic)

questions.q: What pH does a descaler usually have?
questions.a: Lower than 7 (acidic)

questions.q: Why does an acid such as vinegar help against limescale?
questions.a: The acid reacts with lime to form a soluble salt, water and carbon dioxide

questions.q: You pour descaler onto limescale and it starts to fizz. Which gas forms?
questions.a: Carbon dioxide

questions.q: What type of substance is a drain cleaner containing sodium hydroxide solution?
questions.a: A strong base

questions.q: Why are soft drinks bad for your teeth?
questions.a: Soft drinks are acidic and attack the tooth enamel

questions.q: Sal ammoniac (NH<sub>4</sub>Cl) decomposes when heated. What is the reaction equation?
questions.a: NH<sub>4</sub>Cl (s) → NH<sub>3</sub> (g) + HCl (g)

questions.q: What is an emulsion?
questions.a: A mixture in which small droplets of one liquid are spread through another liquid

questions.q: What is an emulsifier?
questions.a: A substance that makes water and oil or fat mix
